title: SDK trace hooks to correlate token-level inference latency with Tempo traces
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add lightweight SDK-level trace hooks in Redwood clients (Python/Node/Go) that emit span annotations for token-level inference events and attach inference request metadata to OTLP spans so Tempo can surface tokenization and KV-cache latency breakdowns. Motivation: customers and oncall frequently need to map per-token service latency spikes back to model/hardware boundaries and prefix/kv cache behavior; current traces only show coarse request spans and miss token-level breakdowns.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (python/node/go) expose an opt-in hook that records token emission start/end and attaches attributes: model_version, sequence_len, kv_cache_hit, batch_id
A server-side OTLP exporter config accepts and forwards the token annotations to Tempo without schema-breaking (attributes limited to 200 chars)
Console trace view surfaces token-level waterfall overlays for requests that opted-in, with latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) per token index
End-to-end test demonstrates a synthetic workload where injected KV-cache misses show a distinct token delay pattern visible in Tempo traces
Feature behind runtime flag and opt-in config; default off for hosted customers to limit trace cardinality
technical_notes: Token-level annotations should be emitted as span events (not new spans) to avoid explosion of span counts
Limit events per request to first 128 tokens and sample 1/10 for longer sequences to bound storage and ingestion costs
Exporter adds a short-lived batching buffer to coalesce token events into existing request span before flush
Ensure tracing headers propagate through proxy/gateway and are preserved when routing to Dedicated/Private backends
implementation_plan: Design SDK hook API and write spec: simple context manager / callback that receives (token_index, token_text, timestamp, kv_hit)
Prototype in python client: emit span.add_event with attribute map; run locally against tempo-dev cluster
Add exporter-side guard in edge collector: strip any token_text > 64 chars and enforce attribute whitelist
Implement sampling/limit config in runtime (env var + console toggle) and wire to SDK via client config
Ship experimental flag to a small internal cohort, collect cost and trace cardinality metrics for two weeks
Iterate on presentation in Console: trace waterfall overlay + toggle to hide/show token-level events
Rollout gradual opt-in across hosted customers; document privacy implications and recommended retention
risks: High cardinality if full token text or large sequences are emitted; mitigated by truncation and sampling
Increased ingestion/cost on Tempo if enabled broadly; require default-off and rate limits
Possible PII exposure from token_text if users send unredacted content; require default stripping of token_text and clear docs
Compatibility issues with older OTLP collectors that drop span events; include fallback to attach aggregate metrics to span attributes
testing_plan: Unit tests for SDK hook API across python/node/go that validate attribute shape and sampling behavior
E2E test: send synthetic requests with deterministic KV-cache misses and assert token-latency pattern appears in Tempo traces
Load test: enable token hooks at 1% sampling across a staging fleet and measure ingestion rate and storage delta
Privacy review test: verify token_text truncation and that retention settings obey console config
notes: 2026-03-02: Spike completed by Marco — prototype in python emits span events to local tempo cluster. Observed ~12% increase in span event count for short sequences (<=64 tokens).

2026-03-05: Design review with PM and Security. Agreed to default strip token_text and only send 'kv_hit' boolean + token index. Security requested retention opt-out and an explicit consent checkbox for hosted customers.
2026-03-08: Requested console mockups from Design; attached waterfall mock. UX suggests collapsing token events by default and showing 'expand tokens' button.
2026-03-09: Marco opened PRs for python SDK and edge collector. Preliminary circleci run shows flaky test for high-concurrency sampling (investigating).
